item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 252324
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located several hundred miles west of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula. The National
Hurricane Center has issued the last advisory on the Remnants of
Julio, located well west of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
A weak and small area of low pressure located well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is producing some
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for gradual development, and a tropical depression
is likely to form late this week or early this weekend while the
system drifts northeastward, then turns to the west-northwest.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week or over the weekend. Some gradual
development is possible by early next week while the system moves
slowly to the west-northwest, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi/Katz/Evans

item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPA32 PHFO 260235
TCPCP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  55
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...LALA EXPECTED TO BECOME A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE IN A COUPLE OF
DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...35.2N 177.6W
ABOUT 540 MI...870 KM N OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 470 MI...760 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...995 MB...29.39 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 35.2 North, longitude 177.6 West. Lala is
moving toward the west-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h) and a slow
west-northwestward to northwestward motion is expected over the
next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some weakening is forecast during the next 48 hours, and Lala
is forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone on Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles (220 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 995 mb (29.39 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 55
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026 
774 
WTPA42 PHFO 260236
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  55
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026
 
Lala continues to exhibit a symmetric convective structure as it 
moves over cooler waters. An ASCAT pass from around 2200 UTC 
captured much of Lala’s inner core and revealed max winds at around 
40 kt. Objective Dvorak estimates range from 45-55 kt, while 
subjective Dvorak estimates from JTWC and HFO reflect a weakening 
trend with a 2.0/2.5 and 2.5/3.0, respectively. Given the quality of 
the ASCAT pass, the initial intensity was held steady at 45 kt. 
 
The motion of the cyclone remains slow as it approaches the 
International Dateline. The initial motion was estimated at 295/5 
kt. Lala continues to be guided to the west-northwest by a high 
pressure ridge centered over the central Pacific, just to the 
northeast of the storm. Global forecast models suggest that the 
ridge will remain stagnant over the next couple of days, which 
should keep Lala moving at a slow speed as it rounds the ridge’s 
westward flank. Eventually, Lala will gain forward speed as it moves 
away from the ridge’s influence and turns more northward. Little 
change was made to the track forecast from the previous advisory.
 
The storm is expected to move over continuously cooling waters 
before encountering a more hostile vertical wind shear environment 
over the next 24 hours. By Thursday, Lala is anticipated to become 
post-tropical, with simulated satellite imagery from the ECMWF 
suggesting that the storm will ultimately dissipate over the 
weekend. Lala’s dissipation time was moved up roughly 24 hours from 
the previous forecast, otherwise the overall intensity trend was 
generally left intact.
